kids: Meet and take photos with the Grinch
Play games, win prizes and try face painting or balloon twisting
See Santa make a special appearance
about: The center's event page promises a whole lot of holiday cheer and prizes for the whole family, with roaming holiday characters on site.
The bonus prize drawing uses a free pre-registration form, with one entry per person, and winners must be present to claim a prize.
The center posts a photo notice: photos and video taken at the event may be used in Tomoka Town Center marketing, and attending counts as consent, including for minors in your care.
The center is open daily and lists its hours on its website, which showed 10 AM to 9 PM on the day this page was checked.
The footer of the event page credits NADG and links to the center's directions, contact, leasing and email update pages.
Barnes and Noble inside the same center holds its own Christmas Celebration the same afternoon, from 2 to 5 PM.
The schedule has a DJ spinning holiday tunes through the afternoon alongside the specialty arts and crafts.
The center's website also carries store hours, directions and a mailing list sign up.
The event page repeats the weather note in plain terms, and points visitors to its Facebook and Instagram pages.
faq: Is the Grinch-Fest free?
Yes. The center calls it a free family event.
What time is it?
Saturday, December 12, 2026, from 11 AM to 4 PM.
When are the raffle drawings?
Prizes are drawn every 10 minutes, with a bonus drawing at noon and the grand prize drawing at 1 PM.
Do I need to register?
Only for the bonus prize drawing, which has a free online registration form.
What if it rains?
The center says weather may change or cancel the plans and to check its social media.
Does Santa attend?
Yes, the center lists a special appearance by Santa.
Where do I park and find the stage?
The event page lists the center address, 1401 Cornerstone Blvd, and a directions link on its site.
Can I take photos?
Yes, and the center warns that its own photos and video may be used in marketing.

How do I reach the store?

Guests are told to bring friends and their best Buddy level enthusiasm, while the property supplies the Christmas cheer.
ONE DAYTONA lists a Wonderland Music Series on the property during November and December, and its calendar had a Home for the Holidays Jingle Jams Thanksgiving Eve special on November 25.

The same property listed a Jeep Beach Toy Drive on November 22 and a Hello Fall Cookie Decorating Workshop on November 24, showing how busy its events calendar is.

December 1, 8 and 15, 2026, each from 6 to 8 PM.

Buddy the Elf joins the evening for North Pole magic.
Where is it?
Inside GameTime, 250 Daytona Blvd, Daytona Beach.

ONE DAYTONA lists dinner and drinks at GameTime.

kids: Join a hands-on children's holiday workshop
Create something special for the season
site: Education Building at Ponce Inlet Lighthouse
about: The lighthouse's flyer lists five workshop dates, starting with Monday, November 23, which has now passed.
Tickets went on sale Monday, October 12 at noon through Lighthouse Locker, and space is capped at 15 participating children per date.
A regional family calendar says each session runs from 11 AM to noon, and the lighthouse phone number is 386-761-1821.
A lighthouse post says children make festive crafts including decorated picture frames, lighthouse ornaments, pinecone decorations and painted sand dollars.
The lighthouse's posted ticket availability said tickets were still available for the majority of the dates.

December 2, 9, 15 and 17, 2026, at 11 AM.

The lighthouse limits it to 15 participating children.

Through Lighthouse Locker, according to the lighthouse.
Where is it held?
The Education Building at the Ponce Inlet Lighthouse, 4931 S. Peninsula Drive.

Friday, December 11, 2026, at 5 PM.

The city lists no set end time.
Where is it?
The Live Oak Center park area in New Smyrna Beach.

Pick a spot along the route near Riverside Park
site: Route starts near Menard-May Park in Edgewater
Passes Riverside Park in New Smyrna Beach
about: Canal Street Historic District describes the parade as a Christmas boat parade on the Intracoastal Waterway at dusk.
The city calendar routes the boats north past Riverside Park, around the North Causeway, The Grille at Riverview and Bouchelle Island, and back toward Riverside Park.
Classic Cars on Canal fills Canal Street from 3 to 6 PM the same afternoon, according to the city calendar.
A regional family calendar lists Edgewater Light Up the Night at Hawks Park on November 28 from 6 to 9 PM, free.
The Canal Street Historic District also keeps a Christmas On Canal page on its site for its other holiday events.
The district runs from a post office box in New Smyrna Beach and lists Facebook and Instagram pages for event updates.
faq: What time is the boat parade?
The district lists dusk on December 12, 2026, and the city calendar lists 6 PM.
Does it cost anything to watch?
No. Watching from the shoreline along the route is free.
Where does it start?
Just south of Menard-May Park in Edgewater, per the city calendar.
Which New Smyrna Beach landmarks does it pass?
Riverside Park, the North Causeway, The Grille at Riverview and Bouchelle Island.
Who lists it?
The Canal Street Historic District and the City of New Smyrna Beach calendar.

kids: Decorate a gingerbread house with edible decorations
Stay for dinner provided by the church
site: First Church DeLand, 135 E Howry Ave
about: The bulletin tags the contest as annual and says houses are provided while families bring their own decorations.
Every decoration must be edible, according to the bulletin, and dinner is provided during the 4 to 6 PM window.
The church lists a Christmas luncheon on Thursday, December 3 at noon with music from the DeLand High School choir, soup and sandwiches, for $8.
Students sell their handmade items in the Building 6 parking lot at 111 S. Alabama Ave on December 4 from 12:30 to 2 PM.
The church takes poinsettia orders until December 7 at $10 each, with pickup after the 5:30 and 7:30 PM Christmas Eve services.
The church office number is 386-734-5113, and the digital bulletin updates weekly on Thursdays.
The church lists a women's Christmas dinner on Monday, December 14, and Impact Wednesday dinners with Alpha sessions through the season.
Traditional worship is at 8 AM and 11 AM and contemporary worship at 9:30 AM on Sundays, so the contest falls after the day's services.
The church's children's ministry rooms are in the LEC, where K through 5th grade meets in Room 121 during the 9:30 service.
The bulletin runs a Bible Challenge reading plan from October 20 to January 1, 2027, which families can follow alongside the contest.
For Christmas Eve, the church lists services at 5:30 PM and 7:30 PM on December 24, with ordered poinsettias handed out afterward.
Gingerbread registration closes on Sunday, December 6, a week before the contest.
The church describes its mission as intentionally sharing Christ's love and salvation.
A Bell Choir rehearsal meets Mondays at 2 PM in the Sanctuary and Chancel Choir rehearses Wednesdays at 6:30 PM.
faq: When is the contest?
Sunday, December 13, 2026, from 4 to 6 PM.
Do we need to sign up?
Yes. The bulletin asks families to register by December 6.
Are the houses provided?
Yes. Bring your own decorations, all of which must be edible.
Is dinner included?
The bulletin says dinner will be provided.
What follows the contest?
An outdoor movie night on the Pumpkin Patch from 6 to 8 PM.
Who runs the contest?
First Church DeLand, a Methodist church at 135 E Howry Ave.
Is the gingerbread edible?
Every decorating element must be edible, according to the bulletin.
How much does it cost to enter?
The bulletin prints no fee for the contest; it asks only for registration by December 6.
What time should we arrive?
The contest starts at 4 PM, and dinner is provided during the 4 to 6 PM window.
Can we bring store bought candy?
Yes, any decoration works as long as it is edible, per the bulletin.
Where do we register?
The bulletin points to the church's connect card and website sign up, and the office is at 386-734-5113.
